quarterly_data.quarter: Dell Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Michael Dell on the supply set-up into 2027, a period the Q2 call did not guide: all of the improvements in the models, particularly from basic LLMs to reasoning to agents, has occurred well within the timeframe required to build a new semiconductor fab, so you just have a structural shortage, probably worse in 2027 than in 2026 from everything that we see. Costs are going up and Dell prices them through; customers move from objecting to price to asking whether Dell can supply them over the next year, two years. Dell says it watches closely for any signs of double ordering or things that are not being utilized, and we don't see that. Deferred demand keeps building behind the shortage: there are 400 million PCs that are over four years old and 1.3 million servers that are 13th generation or older, with customers sweating assets because memory cost has risen.
quarterly_data.figure: structural shortage, probably worse in 2027 than in 2026; 400 million PCs that are over four years old; 1.3 million servers that are 13th generation or older

quarterly_data.quarter: Dell Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: How Dell underwrites neocloud orders, stated explicitly for the first time: the neoclouds have done a very good job finding power and land, and Dell looks THROUGH them to understand where the real demand is coming from - on the other side it is Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Michael Dell says Dell wants to see those contracts, and if they don't have one of those contracts, eh, not interested. Dell also bridges short-term financing to the longer-term sources of capital that want to finance these projects, and introduces neoclouds that are not ready to build their own data centre to partners - a customer arrives saying I need 5,000 Vera Rubin and Dell arranges the rest. He repeats that delivering a massive cluster six weeks ahead of a competitor is worth more to that customer than whatever premium Dell charges.
quarterly_data.figure: neocloud orders require an offtake contract with Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, Google or Meta; example customer request of 5,000 Vera Rubin; six weeks ahead of a competitor

quarterly_data.quarter: Dell Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Sovereign AI sized for the first time: if you take the top 50 countries in the world by GDP, you can find two or three sovereign AI projects in pretty much every one. Sponsors vary - sometimes government, sometimes a telco, sometimes just private industry. Michael Dell says some countries are 12 or 18 months behind US adoption but the activity is sizeable, and maybe half the opportunity is outside the United States. In Dell's segmentation sovereign sits between neocloud and enterprise (with public sector inside it), while enterprise is growing faster but is not as big as neocloud.
quarterly_data.figure: two or three sovereign AI projects in pretty much every one of the top 50 countries in the world by GDP; some 12 or 18 months behind the US; maybe half the opportunity is outside the United States

players.product: PowerEdge XE9680 AI servers & PowerScale storage

quarterly_data.quarter: Dell Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Storage attach and on-prem frontier models: Increasingly, these AI factories have our PowerScale and ObjectScale storage platforms attached to them, and Michael Dell claims Dell is largest there, larger than number 2, number 3, often number 4 combined together in enterprise data storage, citing 26% growth in the last quarter on the pivot to Dell IP storage. New versus the call: The frontier models also want to come on-prem with us - Dell says it is bringing the frontier models on-prem so customers can keep proprietary data in-house, alongside the mix of small, large, open and closed models, and notes 85% of data is still on-prem by various estimates. He flags physical-world AI - robotics, multi-robot agent coordination in factories and transportation - as the next enterprise storage demand driver, on top of networking having to be re-architected and more CPUs being needed for agentic behaviour.
quarterly_data.figure: 26% growth in the last quarter; larger than number 2, number 3, often number 4 combined together; 85% of data is still on-prem
